items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: And Charles Mingus, my influence that I had for playing in his band.

ctx.x: And there you are and I’m trying to think of a question here because it was quite an event. Do you remember how you felt afterwards?

Oh yeah. Because I could see the whole thing going up to that and afterwards and the whole thing. Okay that was the result of the Jazz and People’s Movement. We would go into these studios, Merv Griffin and all these different studios, The Tonight Show and everything, and just start playing New Orleans style music and interrupt their taping. So it went on and Mark — I forget the guy’s name — was part of it and he’s still around. But we would do this Jazz and People’s Movement. So we were trying to get jazz to be…

we were going to play “My Cherie Amour” and we had done that. That’s when he said “Kukumba” and then started with the whole thing. And everybody was just ready. And everything was on the spur of the moment and he introduced everybody later, Archie Shepp and Archie played, then Mingus, and the thing that Mingus and Rahsaan was doing was they played the dozens. And people don’t understand that, that’s when you’re talking back and you’re playing the dozens. Now I won’t even go any deeper than that because most…
